discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived and led the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope. The idea is simple: detect the Cherenkov light from neutrino interactions in natural ice. Carrying it out at the South Pole was a great technical achievement. In 2013 IceCube reported the first evidence for a diffuse flux of extraterrestrial neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, a qualitatively new observation of the Universe. Neutrinos are not deflected by magnetic fields or absorbed by matter, so they come straight from cosmic accelerators. This was followed by the 2017 coincidence of a neutrino with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056, evidence of neutrino emission from the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and a neutrino image of the Galactic plane (2023). These results opened neutrino astronomy and made neutrinos a working messenger in multi-messenger astrophysics. The citation is narrow: the discovery of cosmic high-energy neutrinos.
